Contemporary Issues: Tectonic Environments — a core area of A-Level Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Contemporary Issues: Tectonic Environments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between weather and climate?
options: Weather is short-term atmospheric conditions at a specific time and place; climate is the long-term (typically 30-year) average of weather patterns in a region.
Longshore drift is the rising of sea level over time.
Weather happens outside and climate happens globally.
Weather refers to rain and climate refers to temperature.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a four-figure and six-figure grid reference?
options: Four-figure references identify a 1km square (eastings then northings); six-figure references pinpoint a location within that square to 100m accuracy by adding tenths.
Six-figure references are just longer versions of the same thing.
Longshore drift is the rising of sea level over time.
Four-figure references are for OS maps and six-figure references are for atlases.
Sand moves along the beach because tides pull it sideways.
Four-figure references are for OS maps and six-figure references are for atlases.
The zigzag movement of sediment along a coast caused by waves approaching at an angle (swash up the beach) and gravity returning water perpendicular (backwash).
Longshore drift is the rising of sea level over time.
